patients.label: Case: 27-year-old obese nulliparous woman with prolonged irregular menstrual bleeding, severe anemia and endometrial carcinoma
attribution_limitations: The case text cites Figure 2 for the pipelle sampling result reported as a well-differentiated endometrial endometrioid adenocarcinoma (FIGO grade 1), while the Figure 2 caption names atypical endometrial hyperplasia; the source does not reconcile them.
The discussion says this patient did not receive proper treatment to control endometrial hyperplasia, but the case text reports no hyperplasia diagnosis other than the Figure 2 caption.

The case text says investigations 6 years ago did not yield a diagnosis and the discussion says the initial result revealed no abnormalities; the source does not say whether these are the same investigation or which test was done.
The hormonal intrauterine device inserted in the case text and the LNGIUS in the discussion are not literally identified as the same device.

The discussion says further evaluation was missed as she defaulted follow-up (undated); the case text says she defaulted on her gynecological follow-up in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. The source does not state whether these are the same default.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
The uterus is enlarged, 9.5 cm×5.0 cm. The intrauterine mass size is 6.4 cm×3.0 cm, hyperechoic with mixed echogenicity and extending to the lower part of the uterus.

Figure 2
Atypical endometrial hyperplasia (H&E staining, ×10).

Figure 3
Malignant cell in complex papillary and villoglandular configuration with cribriform architecture, showing crowded, irregular confluent, and back-to-back glands surrounded by desmoplastic stroma (H&E staining, ×20).

limitations: The Figure 2 caption (atypical endometrial hyperplasia) conflicts with the case text citing Figure 2 for the pipelle result (well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma, FIGO grade 1); both are kept as review-only observations and the FIGO grade is not recorded as an include fact.

The discussion sentence that the prolonged interval from symptom onset to cancer may be explained by missed follow-up, the sentence that delays in seeking care resulted in serious outcomes, and the risk statement about obesity are author interpretations or non-specific and are not recorded as separate clinical facts.
Hyperplasia is recorded only as a possible, unconfirmed condition from a discussion sentence.

The discussion sentence that the patient was treated with an LNGIUS and high-dose progesterone refers to this patient (no citation in the sentence) and is recorded in oncology.treatments without a tumor link as its own timeline event; it is not literally identified with the hormonal intrauterine device in the case text, so the two are not merged.
No sex is recorded for the husband (the source prints "His husband"); no supplements and no tables exist; three single-panel figures were viewed in visual.json.
Written informed consent (b00010) is administrative and is not recorded as a fact.

claims.text: A 27-year-old obese, nulliparous woman had a history of prolonged irregular menstrual bleeding since menarche at age 12, with heavy bleeding lasting more than 15 days per cycle from age 15. She did not seek treatment, developed recurrent symptomatic anemia with multiple hospital admissions for blood transfusions over the past 7 years, defaulted on gynecological follow-up in 2020, and subsequently received irregular treatment with hematinic and tranexamic acid. She had been married since 2020 and had not conceived without contraception.
